requirements.requirement: WireGuard tunnel joins node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) private networks so node3 and node4 reach each other by their private addresses (10.10.1.0/24 <-> 10.10.2.0/24)
requirements.summary: wg0 configured on both routers (VyOS native CLI, OPNsense core WireGuard model via config.xml/MVC). Direct bidirectional ping tests from node3 to node4 and vice versa succeeded with 0% loss (cmd-3cc0b8e2852b47e9, cmd-8b950040b94741f1), and tcpdump on node1's eth2/wg0 shows the ICMP traffic entering the tunnel (cmd-2672623f93bd4d3e).

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the two routers travels inside the WireGuard tunnel over the transit network rather than in the clear
requirements.summary: tcpdump captured on node1's transit interface (eth0) during private-network pings shows only encrypted UDP/51820 WireGuard packets between 10.100.190.10 and 10.100.190.11, with no cleartext ICMP visible on the transit link (cmd-edf3955814a94414, cmd-3171d5351ebb4444).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node1 (VyOS) healthy baseline, restart, boot-identity change, recovery
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id and WireGuard/route/ping state captured (cmd-2055f1b6fb314737), reboot issued (cmd-1404f4a8d1f74d93), node became unreachable then returned with a new distinct boot_id and 0-minute uptime (cmd-d49fbcaa191e4836), and wg0 address, peer handshake, static route, and ping to node3 fully recovered post-reboot (cmd-f5d84bf3585f4ed2, cmd-c662c2d4393f4498). Cross-checked against fixed after-executor snapshot boot-identity change.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node2 (OPNsense) healthy baseline, restart, boot-identity change, recovery (including any persistence fix)
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime and WireGuard/route/ping state captured (cmd-b8b20db37c824225). First reboot (cmd-f19b0be942c94952) changed boot time (cmd-b87421a8779d4e18) but exposed a genuine persistence bug: wg0 lost its tunnel address and peer route (cmd-1cb50868d366428f). A second reboot after an initial /etc/rc.local fix (cmd-b0a5491479bf4a25, boot time changed at cmd-d7f98866bca7403d) still showed the address/route missing (cmd-e77b5299c0ea4889), so the executor replaced the fix with the officially supported rc.syshook.d/start hook (cmd-a4d46e4115424a02). A third reboot (cmd-9136be75255846b2, new boot time confirmed at cmd-53b8953455ed4b55) showed wg0's address and route restored automatically without manual intervention (cmd-4322254d9d8e4f97), and bidirectional pings to node3/node4 succeeded shortly after (cmd-ee3581a4ffa44ba2, cmd-f9a3db33108a44d2), confirming the fix was durable across an actual reboot cycle.

Reboot issued and boot_id confirmed changed (cmd-41aba70752614670), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Static IP, route, and ping to node4 fully recovered post-reboot (cmd-b0d9d69402744a47).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: node4 (CentOS) healthy baseline, restart, boot-identity change, recovery
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id, static address, and ping to node3 captured (cmd-bc1fa5c97fcc443a). Reboot issued and boot_id confirmed changed (cmd-e8d39d1a48f542ee), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Static IP, route, and ping to node3 fully recovered post-reboot (cmd-439a26a5d7a44d81).

overall_summary: The executor built a working WireGuard site-to-site tunnel between VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2), joining the 10.10.1.0/24 and 10.10.2.0/24 private networks. Bidirectional connectivity between node3 and node4 by private address is directly demonstrated via ping, and tunnel encapsulation is directly confirmed via tcpdump showing only encrypted UDP/51820 traffic on the transit interface. The mandatory node-restart protocol was completed for all four nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity, service, and connectivity evidence. Node2 (OPNsense) required real iterative debugging — a first reboot exposed a genuine boot-persistence bug in OPNsense's WireGuard service-control script, an intermediate fix attempt still failed on a second reboot, and a final rc.syshook.d hook was verified to work automatically on a third reboot — this is legitimate, transparently-documented remediation rather than a hygiene problem, though it added complexity and repeated reboot cycles. Some low-risk, largely self-cleaned troubleshooting mutations (temporary probe IPs, iterated rc.local drafts) were observed but did not leave meaningful residue.
limitations: Cleanup of temporary ARP-probe IP addresses on node1/node3/node4 sometimes failed with 'address not found' errors rather than explicit successful deletion; the trace cannot fully establish the exact mechanism by which those addresses disappeared (likely superseded by later VyOS commit / NetworkManager reconfiguration), though final interface checks confirm a clean end state.

The node2 restart evidence involved three reboot cycles rather than one; while the final cycle directly demonstrates automatic recovery of the persistence fix, the intermediate failed cycle is itself informative (showing the bug) rather than a failure of the outcome once the final corrected state is considered.

Fixed lifecycle snapshots only cover boot-identity, platform, temp-files, failed-services, listening-sockets, and package-health — they do not directly capture interface/IP state, so cross-checking of network configuration cleanliness relies on the executor's own command outputs rather than the fixed snapshot diff.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor mutations were directly tied to establishing or verifying the tunnel. Some troubleshooting churn occurred but was bounded and largely self-corrected: (1) Temporary probe IPs (192.168.99.x) were added to node1/eth1/eth2, node2/vtnet1/vtnet2, node3/enp8s0, and node4/enp8s0 for ARP-based NIC-pairing discovery (cmd-133b88bd90e24187, cmd-cc4cdbab07e542c6, cmd-4afeecbeb5d44b6e, cmd-a3724f80f9b649f2, cmd-271f5d129c244360, cmd-f173d3423a96444e). Cleanup attempts partly failed with benign errors (cmd-f9768411d26d4529, cmd-0ed16fd3202b4bf0, cmd-6f7e00941b9b4665) because the addresses had already been superseded by later declarative configuration (VyOS commit, NetworkManager reconfiguration); final interface checks (cmd-d1539a7f1f754d29, cmd-8fee789b666a49ee) confirm no residual 192.168.99.x addresses remained. This was a reasonable, low-risk discovery step given ambiguous NIC-to-node mapping, fully resolved in the end. (2) On node2, three iterations of a boot-persistence workaround were attempted before settling on the final fix: an /etc/rc.local script was created twice with slightly different content (cmd-964cfacb2c314940, cmd-21b17b6cb0354c6b, cmd-06cfa03bf0fc4b64, cmd-25ee29321259460b) and then deleted (cmd-a4d46e4115424a02) once the officially supported rc.syshook.d/start/95-antrieb-wg-tunnel hook was adopted — this is troubleshooting churn but it was fully reverted and left no residue. No unsafe exposure, weakened security controls, or damaged package state was observed; the fixed lifecycle diff for node2 shows no unexpected persistent temp-file or listening-socket residue beyond normal reboot artifacts.
